bull_bear.body: Debt reduction priority (target <2x EBITDA in 12-18 months); Dividend INR 4/share recommended; Exploring external capital for Zigly to fund growth without balance sheet strain.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity margin volatility (7-8 new BOPP lines in India next 3 years); Delay in US tariff refund processing; Execution risk in scaling consumer brands (marketing burn); Geopolitical impact on West Asia operations.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume leverage and cost leadership; Cautious on predicting commodity cycles; Aggressive on brand building for consumer verticals; Disciplined on debt and ROCE improvement.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory gains parked in finished goods at port masked some margin benefits in Q4; US tariff refund may require sharing portion with customers who accepted price hikes; Specialty Chemical volume growth (20%) decoupled from revenue growth (10%) due to RM deflation.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the explicit priority: net debt of Rs 1,166 Cr at June 2026 at 2.3x EBITDA versus 2.9x in Jun'25, "targeting below 2.0x within 12-18 months" and "clear focus to reduce net debt substantially in next 2 years".
- Net debt has been broadly flat across the year (Rs 1,140 Cr Jun-25, 1,234 Sep-25, 1,214 Dec-25, 1,159 Mar-26, 1,166 Jun-26) despite a Rs 85 Cr net-working-capital increase from higher raw-material prices post the West Asia war.
- Net debt/equity is 0.7x at Jun-26 and has been stable at 0.7-0.8x through the year, while net worth has grown from Rs 854 Cr in FY21 to Rs 1,676 Cr at Jun'26.
- The framing is a shift from "Investment-led growth" and "Capacity expansion phase" to "Cash generation & value creation" and "Scale, utilization & profitability", with ROCE described as "improving from FY26 levels towards a mid teen steady state as new capacity reaches full utilization".
- A value-unlock event is flagged for the petcare vertical: "Near-term value unlock planned by end of FY27" / "Plan to unlock value in Petcare vertical", with no structure, valuation or counterparty disclosed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- World's largest thermal lamination film producer and second-largest specialty label film producer globally; among top four global players in BOPP specialty films
- Widest product portfolio under one roof combined with customised innovation, allocation flexibility across job lines, scale, global reach and global warehousing facility
- R&D-led moat: advanced R&D centre in Aurangabad, 30+ researchers including PhDs and post-doctoral professionals, six registered patents with eleven more in pipeline (seven India, four overseas)
- De-commoditising product mix: speciality films accounted for 59% of FY26 sales
- Global distribution reach: exports to 100+ countries, ~44% of sales from exports, office presence in 7 countries
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Currency exchange and interest rate volatility — Company's cautionary statement flags changes in currency exchange and interest rates as a factor that could cause actual results to differ significantly from expectations.
- Competitive pressure — Cautionary statement explicitly names competitive pressures as a risk that could affect the Company's business and financial results.
- Macroeconomic, governmental and regulatory changes — General market, macroeconomic, governmental and regulatory patterns, plus regulatory developments, are flagged as factors that could cause actual outcomes to differ from current assessments.
- Counterparty / third-party financial condition risk — Cautionary statement flags changes in the financial condition of third parties doing business with the Company as a risk factor, indicating exposure to customer/supplier/partner credit or solvency issues.
- Technology and technical-advance risk — Technical advances are named among the factors that could cause actual business/financial results to differ from expectations, implying exposure to process or product obsolescence.
- Broad enterprise risk exposure across strategic, financial, liquidity, security, regulatory, legal and reputational categories — The Board-level Risk Management Committee is mandated to oversee strategic, financial, liquidity, security, regulatory, legal, reputational and other risks, indicating these are the categories management considers material enough to require dedicated governance oversight.
- Execution risk on the Filmax Korea joint venture — The 50:50 JV agreement with Filmax Corporation for flexible-packaging distribution, sale and marketing in Korea has been signed but the JV entity 'is in the process of incorporation,' so the anticipated benefits are not yet realised through a formed legal entity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Films: "Largest flexible packaging film producer in India, with BOPP capacity of 277k MT", "Globally amongst top four players in BOPP Specialty films", "Specialty Labels - Second largest player in the world" and "Thermal Lamination Films World's Largest Supplier"; a portfolio slide adds "World's Largest: Thermal Lamination Films & Industrial Application Films".
- The stated arc is "Investment phase -> Deleveraging -> Superior ROCE & scale-up", and a transformation slide contrasts "Predominantly films-led portfolio" vs "Multi-business specialty portfolio" and "Traditional packaging focus" vs "Value-added specialty products".
- Films are said to contribute ~90% of revenue today, with the explicit objective to "Increase contribution from emerging businesses" and to raise non-film EBITDA over three years.
- Export-led: ~50% of revenue from exports, with the films slide citing 80+ countries and the global-footprint slide citing customer presence in 100+ countries; the U.S. and Japan are called premium-realization markets and "~Majority of exports comes from Specialty Films".
- Each engine has a named role: Films = "Core cash-generating platform driving scale and global leadership"; Specialty Chemicals = "High-margin innovation business supporting profitability and ROCE improvement"; Plastech = complementary value-added rigid packaging; Cosmo Consumer = premium branded film solutions; Zigly = consumer-facing integrated pet-care ecosystem.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Shareholding] Jun-26 pattern: Promoter 40.78%, Institutional 3.93%, Non-Institutional 54.18%, ESOP Trust 1.11% - institutional ownership is notably thin.
- [Tariffs] "US Business Margin expansion post tariff normalization" is listed as a short-term growth driver, implying current US-business margins are tariff-depressed; the deck gives no tariff quantum or timeline.
- [Geopolitics] Raw-material prices rose "post the West Asia conflict", adding Rs 85 Cr to net working capital - the named reason net debt did not fall this quarter.
- [Market context] Addressable markets as stated by the deck: India BOPP ~900K MT pa / Rs 13,000 Cr growing 8-10%; rigid packaging Rs 10,000 Cr growing 10%+; India pet care Rs 25,000 Cr growing 22% pa; India heat-control film ~Rs 1,000 Cr pa growing ~8% with only two producers in India (incl. Cosmo); India PPF ~Rs 500 Cr growing 30% YoY at 1-2% penetration vs ~15% in China.
- [One-offs] Cosmo Plastech's reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA includes a one-time government incentive of Rs 2.4 Cr; excluding it, normalized EBITDA is 7%. FY25 specialty-chemicals EBITDA of Rs 33 Cr is also stated as excluding a one-time incentive.

business.body: Cosmo First (formerly Cosmo Films, est. 1981) manufactures BOPP, BOPET, thermal lamination, coated specialty, metalised and CPP flexible packaging films for FMCG brands, flexible packaging converters, label manufacturers and channel partners in India and 100+ export countries. The Company has diversified beyond films into specialty chemicals (coating chemicals, masterbatch, adhesives) under Cosmo Speciality Chemicals, end-to-end rigid packaging under Cosmo Plastech, window films/paint protection films under the Cosmo Consumer division (Cosmo Sunshield, Cosmo PPF, Cosmo Guard), and a direct-to-consumer pet care vertical under the Zigly brand.

outlook.body: Zigly spin-off/external funding planned FY27; US/Europe expansion for Auto Care films (currently <20% util); Specialty Chemicals volume growth (20% YoY) masked by lower RM prices; Tariff refund >INR 60 Cr expected over 6-12 months.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Growth anchored in specialisation across five verticals with distinct identities under one roof — Cosmo Films (flexible packaging), Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging), Cosmo Speciality Chemicals, Cosmo Consumer (window films/PPF), and Zigly (pet care) — sharing a common foundation of innovation and customer focus
- Continue to de-commoditise the flagship film business by increasing focus on speciality films and sustained R&D investment, particularly on sustainability, to drive long-term sustainable growth
- Maximise returns from the ₹1,200 crore strategic capital investments undertaken over the last three years, with each business vertical targeted on enhancing intrinsic value through disciplined emphasis on high-margin opportunities and superior ROCE
- Strengthen financial resilience by reducing corporate net debt substantially over the next 2 years
- Expand global footprint through international partnerships and operations — 50:50 joint venture with Filmax Corporation (South Korea) and expanded North American finishing operations at Carol Stream, Illinois
- Advance toward a sustainable, green future by developing films from mono-material structures that are easily recyclable, helping customers reduce their carbon footprint
- In Speciality Chemicals, focus each of the three verticals (coating chemicals, masterbatch, adhesives) on niche specialties addressing current industry problem areas or offering significantly superior products versus what is currently available
- In Cosmo Plastech, focus on establishing direct-to-brand partnerships with leading FMCG companies rather than intermediated sales
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Cosmo First has invested Rs 1,180 crore over the last three years in multiple growth projects spanning BOPP, CPP & Polyester lines, Metallizers, Coating lines, Window/PPF films, Zigly and Rigid Packaging. During the year the Company commissioned a state-of-the-art 10.4-meter, 5-layer BOPP film line with annual capacity of 81.2 KMT (one of the highest-capacity lines globally), taking total BOPP capacity to approximately 277 KMT per annum across 10 lines, up from 196 KMT (9 lines) a year earlier. Coated Specialty Films capacity was similarly expanded to 45,000 MT (10 lines) from 36,000 MT (8 lines). The Company also strengthened its global footprint via a 50:50 joint venture with Filmax Corporation (Korea) for marketing and distribution of flexible packaging products, launched the Cosmo Consumer vertical (Cosmo Sunshield window films, now in 100+ Indian cities/towns, and Cosmo PPF paint protection films), and grew Zigly's pet-care experience-centre network to over 40 stores as of March 2026, including the acquisition of two veterinary hospitals (Mumbai and Bengaluru). Cosmo First holds six registered patents with eleven more in the pipeline (seven in India, four overseas).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic demand and supply scenario for flexible packaging is expected to remain favourable in the coming years, aided by e-commerce growth, food & beverage demand, sustainability/recyclability trends, and urbanisation
- Speciality chemicals demand supported by rapid urbanisation, government infrastructure programmes (e.g. Smart Cities Mission), rising middle-class disposable incomes, EV adhesive demand and renewable energy installations
- Rigid packaging growth driven by rising demand for packaged goods and beverages and by deeper direct engagement with leading FMCG brand customers
- Window/sun-control film segment: with only two domestic manufacturers of window films in India, management views this as a significant high-margin growth opportunity; demand also driven by rising awareness of energy efficiency and sustainable building materials
- Pet care segment demand supported by premiumisation and the largely non-discretionary, resilient nature of pet-related spending, alongside rising pet ownership in India
- Speciality films sales mix reached 59% of FY26 sales, reflecting a continuing shift away from commodity films toward higher-margin speciality products
- FY26 consolidated EBITDA improvement attributed to higher volumes following commissioning of new BOPP and CPP lines, growth in speciality films, and improved profitability in the specialty chemicals business
- BOPET line specialty product pipeline: company is introducing new specialty products including window films, security films, PET-G films, and others
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Cosmo First posted strong Q4FY26 volume growth (41% YoY) and EBITDA expansion (53% YoY) driven by new capacity commissioning and specialty mix, though PAT was muted by one-off tax reversals. The thesis pivots from CAPEX execution to 'sweating assets' with a clear path to debt reduction (<2x EBITDA) and margin expansion as new verticals (Zigly, Plastech) approach breakeven and US tariff refunds (~INR 60 Cr) flow through.

meta.thesis: Cosmo First posted strong Q4FY26 volume growth (41% YoY) and EBITDA expansion (53% YoY) driven by new capacity commissioning and specialty mix, though PAT was muted by one-off tax reversals. The thesis pivots from CAPEX execution to 'sweating assets' with a clear path to debt reduction (<2x EBITDA) and margin expansion as new verticals (Zigly, Plastech) approach breakeven and US tariff refunds (~INR 60 Cr) flow through.
